creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`every_pane_reports_its_agent_state_without_being_attached_to` failed once during a full `./dev` run, timing out at its 10s deadline, and passed immediately when rerun alone. Nothing about it changed; what changed is how many daemons the suite now starts at once - two more daemon-backed test binaries landed with the typing settings and the presentation round trip, and cargo runs test binaries in parallel.

This matters more here than it would elsewhere. "Green suite means it works" is a founding desideratum and Muster is built largely by agents, so a suite that fails once in a while teaches everyone to rerun rather than to read - which is how a real regression gets waved through.

Worth working out before adding more:

- **How many daemons a full run has in flight**, and whether the 10s deadlines are near the edge or miles from it. A number, not a guess.
- **Whether the deadlines are the right lever at all.** A timeout raised until it stops failing is a timeout that no longer catches a hang.
- **Whether daemon-backed binaries should be serialized** against each other rather than each being cheap. They are the slow tier already, and a run that is a few seconds longer and never lies is the better trade.
title: 🎲 The daemon-backed suite can lose a race to itself
